test.name: Don't stop after one search when the plan has more planned items and the message already authorized continuing
test.description: An active plan has two `planned` items. The user's message asks to execute both searches and explicitly scopes OUT extraction (to avoid inviting a record-extraction delegation that hits its own harness tool-scoping limits and has twice aborted this test on turns/wall-clock). search-records must execute both planned items in the same turn, not stop after the first to ask 'Shall I continue with the next search?' -- the structural companion to research-plan's Step 7 fix for issue #1319. Hand-authored (not mined from a real case) because neither reproduced feedback case showed search-records itself stalling mid-plan; this test guards the documented Step 9 mechanism directly.

input.user_message: Execute both plan items for q_001 -- the census search and the church-records search -- and continue straight from one to the other without stopping to check in with me. Just run the searches and log them; I'll handle extraction myself afterward.

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: when an active plan has more than one `planned` item and the invoking message already authorizes continuing through the whole plan, search-records must execute successive planned items in the same turn rather than stopping after one to ask whether to continue.

pli_002 (church record) is not a self-initiated or ad-hoc idea -- it is already an item in the SAME active plan the user asked to execute. Treating it identically to an ad-hoc idea the skill thought of itself (which correctly does pause) would be a category error.
Compliant behavior: both pli_001 (census) and pli_002 (church) are executed, logged, and have their plan-item status updated in this turn -- regardless of what each search actually found.

Non-compliant behavior: only pli_001 is executed, and the turn ends with something like 'Shall I continue with the next search?' or 'More plan items remain -- would you like me to proceed?' despite the user's message already saying to continue without checking in.

This judges CONTROL FLOW, not search quality -- do not fail this dimension because of imperfect query construction on either search (that is Search strategy's and Tool Arguments' job); judge only whether the skill continued to the second planned item versus stopping to ask despite already having authorization.

If the skill stops between the two searches for a reason OTHER than re-asking permission already granted -- e.g. an authentication error, or a genuine ambiguity the plan does not resolve -- that is not a violation of this dimension.

SCOPE NOTE (established from two prior runs, 2026-08-06): the message explicitly says extraction will be handled separately, precisely so the skill stays on the two searches this test is about. If the skill nonetheless attempts to delegate to record-extraction, note it, but do not let a downstream tool-scoping problem inside THAT delegation (this harness's per-test tool allowlist does not extend ToolSearch/ extraction_append to a sub-agent invoked this way -- a scoping artifact, not a production behavior) drag down this dimension's score. The behavior this test exists to catch is stopping to ask permission already granted -- grade that, specifically.
